oidc_jwt.description: SPIFFE JWT SVIDs and Kubernetes service account tokens can be reused multiple times.
oidc_jwt.source: SPIFFE and Kubernetes identity provider documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Replay of the same upstream assertion is documented as possible and should not be flagged as a freshness bug by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token rotation may be disabled by client policy, so refresh responses may not return a new refresh token.
oidc_jwt.note: Lack of refresh token rotation is documented as configurable behavior, not automatically a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT-based assertions or tokens may be reusable unless a specific replay-prevention feature is enabled; stateless JWT replay is not generally tracked.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows and broker/client assertion reuse documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token for ordinary stateless JWT bearer usage unless the specific context is client assertions with reuse disabled or another one-time artifact such as authorization code.

oidc_jwt.description: Some externally issued assertions or tokens can be reusable depending on configuration, and Keycloak documents explicit reuse allowance for client assertions.
oidc_jwt.note: Replay acceptance may be configured behavior rather than a freshness bug.

oidc_jwt.description: TOTP codes can be reused within the valid time interval unless reusable-code policy is disabled accordingly; TOTP does not remember used passwords by design for efficiency.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat TOTP reuse within the validity window as a generic replay vulnerability without considering OTP policy settings.

oidc_jwt.description: The requesting frontend client is not automatically added to the access token aud claim.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of the client itself in aud is by design unless an Audience mapper adds it.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo and token claims depend on linked default/optional client scopes and user permission to use those scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing claims in UserInfo are often due to scope configuration, not authorization bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: Brokered usernames are lower-cased unless Case-sensitive username is enabled on the identity provider.
oidc_jwt.note: Case-folding collisions can be by design under default broker settings and should be tested with the toggle in mind.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo and token claims depend on linked client scopes, optional scope requests, and mapper configuration.
oidc_jwt.source: Client scopes and token role mappings documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Missing claims or groups in UserInfo may reflect scope/mapping configuration rather than identity loss or authorization failure.

oidc_jwt.description: If PKCE method is left blank on the client, PKCE is not required though it may still be used when supplied.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing code_verifier acceptance is by design unless the client is configured to require PKCE.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Authorization Code Flow temporary codes are one-time and short-lived. For I2/I3 tests involving code replay or code injection, the same authorization code MUST be reused exactly once for the attack attempt; any second successful exchange would be anomalous, while a failed second exchange is by design.

PKCE method semantics: if client PKCE method is blank, Keycloak does not require PKCE, though PKCE may still be used. For OIDC flow tests that expect PKCE enforcement, the client/application MUST be configured with PKCE method S256 or plain; otherwise missing code_verifier is accepted by design and causes false positives.

Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching by default. Wildcards are only supported at the end of the URL pattern, and wildcard matching is disabled when the passed redirect URI contains userinfo or parent-directory traversal (/../). For redirect_uri mismatch tests, use exact registered URIs unless explicitly testing the documented trailing-wildcard behavior.

For RP-initiated logout with post_logout_redirect_uri, Keycloak requires either client_id or id_token_hint to be included, and post_logout_redirect_uri must match one of the client's Valid Post Logout Redirect URIs. Missing these parameters causes logout redirect failures by design.

OIDC broker issuer validation is only performed when the Identity Provider configuration includes Issuer. For I1 trust-anchor-substitution and issuer-validation tests against brokered OIDC IdPs, the broker configuration MUST set Issuer explicitly; otherwise issuer comparison is skipped.

OIDC broker signature validation is only performed when Validate Signatures is ON. For I1 alg_none, resign_attacker_key, kid_injection, and trust_anchor_substitution tests against brokered OIDC IdPs, the broker configuration MUST enable Validate Signatures and provide trust material via JWKS URL or Validating Public Key; otherwise signature checks may be skipped.

When broker OIDC signature validation uses JWKS URL, Keycloak caches the external IdP public key for performance. For I3 signing-key-rotation tests, the fuzzer MUST account for key caching and verify that a fresh login after trust rotation is evaluated after cache refresh/propagation, otherwise stale acceptance may reflect cache timing rather than incoherent policy application.

Client assertion reuse behavior is configurable on OIDC identity providers. By default, a client assertion cannot be used multiple times; if Allows client assertions to be re-used is enabled, replay becomes allowed by configuration. For I2 replay tests involving federated client assertions, record this setting and do not flag replay as a bug when reuse is explicitly enabled.

Client assertion audience semantics can be non-standard when Allows Client ID as audience for assertions is enabled. In that mode, the configured client ID becomes the only valid audience instead of token-url/issuer-url. For I1/I5 audience-binding tests on federated client assertions or JWT authorization grants, the fuzzer MUST align the assertion aud with the configured mode or results will be misinterpreted.

Keycloak documents that stateless JWT-style assertions such as SPIFFE JWT SVIDs and Kubernetes service account tokens can be reused multiple times. Replay of the same assertion is therefore not, by itself, an I2 vulnerability in these contexts; treat it as by-design unless a one-time-use mechanism is explicitly configured elsewhere.

For token freshness controls, include a control login using a valid token alongside expired/future-token attacks. Keycloak documents exp/nbf-sensitive flows and multiple timeout layers; without a control request, a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken client/application setup.

Client scopes and role scope mappings determine effective permissions as an intersection. Roles in issued tokens are the intersection of user-assigned roles and the client's permitted role scope mappings. For I5 authorization-escalation tests, do not treat missing roles as a bug unless the role is both assigned to the user and allowed by the client scope configuration.

Client scope permission semantics: if a client scope has role scope mappings, a user may use that scope only when there is an intersection between the user's roles and the scope's roles. If no intersection exists, the scope and its mappers are omitted from the token. For I5 scope-escalation tests, ensure the test user is actually permitted to use the requested scope before interpreting omissions as enforcement failures.

Audience behavior is mapper-driven. The frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience. Audience claims are added through Audience Resolve or Audience protocol mappers/client scopes. For I5 audience tests, configure audience mappers explicitly; absence of aud for the requesting client is by design.

Downscoping on token exchange is only enforced when the client policy executor downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer is applied. For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST know whether this executor is active; without it, requesting broader scopes may be permitted by configuration rather than indicating a vulnerability.

Keycloak documents a client policy executor that restricts scopes granted in standard token exchange to those present in the initial subject_token, except default scopes with include in token scope=false. For I5 token exchange tests under this policy, do not flag retention of such invisible compulsory scopes as escalation.

Sender-constrained mTLS access tokens cannot be used as subject_token in standard token exchange. If a client has OAuth 2.0 Mutual TLS Certificate Bound Access Tokens enabled, token_exchange tests using that token as subject_token are invalid and must not be interpreted as audience or exchange failures.

Default ACR Values do not reliably enforce a required authentication level. Users can override them with acr_values or claims. For I5/step-up tests, use Minimum ACR Value or verify the returned acr claim; do not assume default ACR configuration alone enforces stronger authentication.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout (30 minutes by default), and other browser tabs may automatically restart authentication after one tab succeeds. For I3 state/session-binding tests, bind observations to the same live authentication session and avoid interpreting automatic browser-tab restarts as session confusion.

Numeric sentinel: Password policy Hashing iterations uses -1 as a sentinel meaning use the algorithm default, not literal negative one. Current documented defaults are argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000. Never assume -1 disables hashing iteration checks.

Numeric sentinel: Maximum Authentication Age password policy uses 0 to mean always require re-authentication before password update, not 'use default' or 'disable'. Tests that set this value to 0 must expect the strictest behavior.
Numeric sentinel: User session count limiter uses 0 to disable the session-count check for both realm and client session limits, not literal zero allowed sessions. Do not interpret 0 as deny-all.

Numeric sentinel: WebAuthn Timeout uses 0 to delegate timeout behavior to the authenticator/browser implementation, not immediate timeout and not disabled authentication. Timing tests must not assume deterministic zero-second expiry.

Numeric sentinel: Rotated Secret Expiration uses 0 to remove the old secret immediately during client secret rotation. Secret Expiration and Rotated Secret Expiration are in seconds and rotation only occurs on client update/regenerate actions, not automatically in the background.

Numeric sentinel: CIBA Expires In defaults to 120 seconds and Interval defaults to 5 seconds when not explicitly configured. Polling tests must respect the configured/default interval and expiry window or failures may be due to policy timing rather than security enforcement.

Matching semantics: Valid Redirect URIs support exact case-sensitive matching, with only trailing wildcard patterns documented. For multi-URI tests, do not use '*' as a generic wildcard except where the platform explicitly allows full wildcard; exact-match semantics otherwise apply.

Matching semantics: Essential claim value in identity provider configuration supports regular expression format, while Essential claim name matching is case-sensitive by claim name. For I5 claim-binding tests, distinguish regex-enabled value matching from exact claim-name matching.

Matching semantics: Advanced Claim to Group mapper supports exact claim-value matching unless Regex Claim Values is enabled. For multi-identity I4 tests, if multiple different claim values must match the same mapper, the fuzzer MUST enable regex mode explicitly; otherwise values are exact-match only.

Matching semantics: Regex-based authorization policy uses Java regular expressions against the target claim. For I5 tests, regex behavior is explicit here and should not be generalized to other claim-binding settings that lack a regex toggle.

Claim value typing: pushed claims to the token endpoint for UMA authorization must be a BASE64-encoded JSON object where each claim value is an array of strings. Non-string or non-array claim values are invalid for this API and should not be used for numeric coercion tests here.

Authorization endpoint requests that expect redirects MUST use follow_redirects=false. The authorization endpoint returns browser redirects, and following them in the executor will collapse multi-step flow state and break I3 testing.

For token endpoint requests, content type MUST be application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Keycloak documents the token, revocation, broker token v2, and introspection style endpoints as form-encoded OAuth requests; sending JSON will fail or be misinterpreted.

PKCE matching semantics: client PKCE method is configured as exact enum values blank|S256|plain. Blank means PKCE is optional, not disabled if parameters are present. For pkce_skip and pkce_not_required_public_client tests, do NOT assume PKCE is enforced unless the client explicitly requires S256 or plain.

For I3 redirect/code binding tests, authorization code is one-time and short-lived by design. Reusing the same code should fail and is not evidence of a bug; valid coherence tests must compare behavior before and after config change using fresh authorization requests.

Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching, with wildcard support only at the end of the URL pattern. Wildcards are not general globbing. For redirect_uri_mismatch and related tests, use exact registered redirect_uri values unless intentionally testing the documented trailing-wildcard behavior.

For I4 multi-identity scenarios involving redirect URIs, do NOT set Valid Redirect URIs to '*' unless intentionally testing insecure redirect configuration. '*' allows any http/https redirect URI and changes the security model, causing false positives unrelated to identity binding.

OIDC broker issuer validation is only performed against the configured Issuer field. For I1 trust_anchor_substitution and issuer-validation tests against external OIDC identity providers, configure the broker IdP Issuer explicitly; otherwise issuer comparison may not be enforced as intended by the test.

OIDC broker signature validation is conditional. Validate Signatures must be ON, and either JWKS URL or Validating Public Key must be configured. Without this, tests such as resign_attacker_key, kid_injection, and trust_anchor_substitution can pass trivially because signature verification was not enabled.

When Validate Signatures is ON and Use JWKS URL is enabled, Keycloak caches the external IdP public key. For jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, allow for cache refresh behavior and ensure the second login occurs after trust material is updated in Keycloak; otherwise stale-key acceptance/rejection may reflect cache timing rather than I3 failure.

Validating Public Key Id semantics: if Use JWKS URL is OFF and Validating Public Key Id is not specified, the configured validating public key is used for all requests regardless of kid. For kid_injection tests, set a specific Validating Public Key Id when testing kid enforcement; otherwise kid is effectively ignored by design.

Client assertions reuse behavior is configurable for brokered OIDC providers. By default, a client assertion cannot be used multiple times; enabling 'Allows client assertions to be re-used' changes replay semantics. For I2 replay tests involving client assertions, record whether this option is enabled before interpreting reuse as a vulnerability.

Allows Client ID as audience for assertions is a non-standard mode. If enabled, client assertions and JWT authorization grants may validate audience against client_id instead of token-url/issuer-url. For I1/I5 audience-binding tests, disable this option unless the test explicitly targets this non-standard behavior.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control login using a valid token in the same realm/client configuration. A failed attack token alone cannot distinguish broken setup from correct time validation.

Refresh token rotation has sentinel-like behavior at configuration level: enabling 'Revoke Refresh token' makes refresh tokens one-time-use; client policy executor 'suppress-refresh-token-rotation' disables rotation and later refresh responses may not return a new refresh token. Do not assume refresh rotation is always active.

Client secret rotation numeric sentinel: Rotated Secret Expiration value 0 means the old secret is immediately removed during rotation, not 'use default'. Secret Expiration and Rotated Secret Expiration are literal seconds. Tests that rely on overlap between old and new secrets must avoid 0 for rotated-secret expiration.
Password policy numeric sentinel: Hashing iterations value -1 means use the algorithm default iteration count, not disable hashing iterations. Do not treat -1 as zero or disabled in setup validation.

Maximum Authentication Age password policy sentinel: value 0 means the user must always re-authenticate before password update, not 'use default' or 'disable'. This matters for flows that trigger password-update actions during authentication.

Authentication session timeout is finite and defaults to about 30 minutes. Multi-tab/browser-flow behavior may automatically restart authentication in other tabs after one tab succeeds. For I3 state_swap and session-bound flow tests, isolate browser sessions and do not rely on parallel tabs in the same browser profile.

Authentication session sub-session limit sentinel: authSessionsLimit default is 300 sub-sessions per root authentication session; when the limit is reached, the oldest sub-session is removed. High-volume authorization-start fuzzing in one browser session can evict earlier states and create false I3 failures.

User session count limiter sentinel: realm/client session limit value 0 disables that check, it does not mean zero sessions allowed. If session-limit authenticators are configured in the realm, tests must account for possible denial or oldest-session termination unrelated to token correctness.

Role scope mappings and client scopes constrain permissions by intersection. Access token roles are the intersection of user roles and client role-scope mappings/client scopes. For I5 escalation tests, absence of a role in the token may be due to scope filtering rather than a failed login or identity issue.

Client scope permission semantics are intersection-based: if a client scope has role scope mappings, a user must have at least one intersecting role or the scope is not applied at all. For I5 scope-escalation tests, missing claims may be by design because the user is not permitted to use the requested client scope.

Organization scope request semantics are exact, not wildcard globbing except for the documented literal forms organization, organization:<alias>, and organization:*. For I4/I5 tests involving organization claims, use only these documented forms; arbitrary wildcard patterns are not supported.

Case-sensitive username behavior for brokered identities is configurable. If 'Case-sensitive username' is disabled, brokered usernames are lower-cased when federating users. For I4 case_confusion tests, this lowercasing is by design and must be accounted for before flagging identity collapse.

Essential claim matching for brokered identity providers uses case-sensitive claim-name matching and regex-capable claim-value matching. For multi-identity I4 scenarios, do NOT set Essential claim value to '*' unless you intend regex semantics; exact/wildcard assumptions from other platforms do not apply.

Regex-based policy and Advanced Claim to Group mapper explicitly support regex matching only when configured. If regex mode is disabled, values must match exactly. For I4 multi-identity tests, omit exact-match claim constraints rather than using '*' as a wildcard when regex mode is not enabled.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on claim-based matching, documentation does not specify cross-type coercion guarantees for JWT claim values in broker essential-claim checks or authorization regex policies. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly (e.g., bound integer N vs float N+0.7) and treat acceptance as potential type-confusion behavior rather than assuming stringification.

The frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience by default. For audience_mismatch and cross-provider audience tests, do not assume aud contains client_id unless an Audience or Audience Resolve mapper adds it.

Hardcoded and audience-resolve mappers add audiences to access tokens only by default, while ID tokens typically contain only the client ID audience. For I1/I5 audience tests, use the access token as the security artifact for resource-server audience checks, not the ID token.

Token exchange downscoping can be enforced by client policy executor 'downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer'. When enabled, requested scopes must be a subset of scopes in the presented JWT subject_token/assertion, except invisible compulsory default scopes. For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, determine whether this executor is active before interpreting rejection as a bug.

Sender-constrained mTLS tokens cannot be used as subject_token in standard token exchange. For token_exchange tests, do not use mTLS-bound access tokens as subject_token or failures will be by design.

Authorization endpoint requests that include kc_idp_hint or a configured default identity provider may be redirected to an external IdP instead of showing the local login form. For deterministic OIDC tests against Keycloak as OP, omit kc_idp_hint unless the test explicitly targets broker behavior.

PKCE method blank means PKCE is optional, not disabled. If the client sends PKCE parameters, Keycloak can use them, but it will not require them unless PKCE method is set to S256 or plain. For OIDC flow security tests, configure the client to require PKCE explicitly; otherwise missing-code_verifier results are by design and not evidence of a bypass.

Authorization code flow temporary codes are one-time and short-lived. Reusing the same code is expected to fail. For I3 flow-coherence tests, distinguish code replay rejection from session-binding issues by using a fresh control authorization code for each exchange attempt.

Refresh token rotation is configurable. When 'Revoke Refresh token' is enabled, an already-used refresh token becomes invalid after use; when refresh token rotation is suppressed by client policy, subsequent refresh responses may not return a new refresh token. Do not assume a stable refresh-token lifecycle across clients.

OIDC client scope application is permission-gated. If a client scope has role scope mappings, it only applies when the user has an intersecting role. Missing claims or audiences may therefore be caused by scope permission filtering rather than a token issuance bug. For I5 tests, ensure the test user is permitted to use the requested client scope.

The frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token aud claim. Access-token audience is typically derived from audience mappers or client roles, while the ID token audience is the client ID. For audience-binding tests, inspect access_token aud, not id_token aud, and configure audience mappers or scopes explicitly.

Token exchange downscoping can be enforced by client policy. When the downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer executor is active, requested scopes in token exchange are restricted to scopes already present in the subject_token, except invisible compulsory scopes. For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, first determine whether this executor is enabled; rejection of expanded scope is expected when it is.

Client secret rotation supports up to two concurrently active secrets. Rotations do not happen automatically in the background; they occur on client update, regenerate-secret, or explicit admin REST rotation. For I3 config-change tests involving client secrets, trigger an update/rotation action before expecting old-secret rejection.

Hashing iterations numeric sentinel: password policy value -1 means use the algorithm default iteration count, not zero iterations and not disabled. Do not treat -1 as disabling hashing cost enforcement.
Maximum Authentication Age numeric sentinel: password policy value 0 means the user must always re-authenticate before password update. It is a strict setting, not 'use default' and not disabled.
User session limits numeric sentinel: max sessions value 0 disables that session-limit check. It does not mean zero sessions allowed. If testing session-limit behavior, configure a positive integer.

Authentication session sub-session limit numeric sentinel: authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 authentication sub-sessions per root authentication session; when the limit is reached, the oldest sub-session is removed. Multi-tab browser tests can be affected by this eviction behavior and should avoid creating excessive parallel auth attempts.

Authentication sessions usually expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. In multi-tab flows, other tabs may restart authentication automatically after one tab succeeds, but expired authentication sessions can cause protocol-specific errors. For I3 state/session tests, keep flows within login-timeout windows and avoid relying on stale browser tabs.

When Keycloak acts as an OIDC broker consuming external ID Tokens, issuer validation only occurs against the configured 'Issuer' field. If that field is unset, the documentation does not state that issuer comparison is enforced. For I1 trust-anchor-substitution tests against brokered OIDC IdPs, configure Issuer explicitly; otherwise acceptance may reflect missing configuration rather than a validation bypass.

When Keycloak acts as an OIDC broker, signature validation of external ID Tokens only occurs if 'Validate Signatures' is ON. If OFF, signature verification is not performed. For I1 alg_none, resign_attacker_key, kid_injection, and trust_anchor_substitution tests against brokered OIDC IdPs, enable Validate Signatures and configure JWKS URL or validating public key first.

Brokered OIDC key validation may use cached public keys from the external IdP. After key rotation, Keycloak may continue using cached keys until refresh. For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests against brokered OIDC IdPs, force a fresh validation path or allow for cache refresh behavior before concluding stale trust acceptance.

Brokered OIDC client assertions are single-use by default. If 'Allows client assertions to be re-used' is enabled, replay of the same client assertion becomes allowed by configuration. For replay tests in federated client authentication, check this setting before treating assertion reuse as a vulnerability.

Brokered OIDC essential-claim matching uses a claim name plus a value that supports regular expression format. For multi-identity I4 tests, do not assume wildcard semantics unless you intentionally provide a regex. If you need multiple different identities to pass the same broker constraint, either omit essential-claim filtering or use an explicit regex that matches all intended values.

Organization and broker flows can auto-link or auto-create users depending on First Login Flow configuration. Automatically linking existing accounts is explicitly documented as dangerous in generic environments. For I4 principal-binding tests, avoid flows using 'Automatically Set Existing User' or other auto-linking authenticators unless the test explicitly targets account-linking behavior.

Case-sensitive username handling for brokered identities is configurable. If 'Case-sensitive username' is disabled, brokered usernames are lower-cased before federation, while server usernames are always lower-case. For I4 case_confusion tests, treat Admin vs admin collapsing as by-design when case-sensitive username is disabled.

Organization group mapping via Advanced Claim to Group supports exact matching by default and regex matching only when 'Regex Claim Values' is enabled. For I4 multi-identity or wildcard scenarios, do not set '*' expecting wildcard behavior unless regex mode is enabled; otherwise values must match exactly.

Group-based authorization policy reads groups either from a configured token claim or from realm configuration if Groups Claim is unset. For I5 group-policy tests, ensure the intended source is configured; otherwise policy evaluation may use stored realm memberships instead of token claims, leading to false conclusions about claim handling.

Regex-based authorization policy target claims support dot notation and array indexing into JSON claims. This is regex matching, not exact matching. For I5 claim-binding tests using regex policies, broad patterns may intentionally match multiple values and should not be treated as accidental over-authorization.

Role-based authorization policy defaults to checking only roles available from the token. If 'Fetch Roles' is enabled, the policy ignores token roles and checks any role associated with the user instead. For I5 authorization-binding tests, verify whether Fetch Roles is enabled before concluding that extra roles were granted by the token.

For token freshness tests (expired_token, future_token, nbf), include a control login using a valid token or valid flow parameters alongside the attack case. Without a control, a failed login may reflect client misconfiguration, missing scopes, or broker setup issues rather than time-claim enforcement.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
